newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's SAA to be privatised in '97-paper.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's SAA to be privatised in '97-paper.

text.p: The government plans to find a strategic equity partner for South African Airways (SAA) this year, Business Day newspaper said on Wednesday.
Until now the government has said the privatisation of the national carrier would be carried out before the middle of next year.

The paper also quoted transport director-general Khetso Gordhan as saying state-owned domestic airline Sun Air would be completely privatised within six months. Advisers to government on this process were appointed earlier this month.
Sun Air is one of seven public sector corporations Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau has said will be at least partly privatised by the end of 1997.
Those to be fully privatised are Sun Air, tourist resort group Aventura, mining group Alexcor and transport group Autonet.
Strategic equity stakes are to be sold in telecommunications utility Telkom, the Airports Company which runs South Africa's major airports and forestry group Safcol.

The UK's Virgin Atlantic VAA.CN has shown an interest in taking a 25 percent stake in Sun Air, the maximum allowed under government's restructuring programme. It has already entered into a code share agreement with Sun Air.
